meta.name: Azure DevOps Server (on-premises)
meta.description: Connects the Integrations Hub to a self-hosted Azure DevOps Server collection: team projects, work items and Git repositories.

connector.name: Azure DevOps Server (on-premises)
connector.description: Team projects, work items (two-way, with parents and comments) and Git repository status from a self-hosted Azure DevOps Server, or its 2022, 2020 or 2019 release.

config.collectionUrlHint: The project collection as it appears in your browser, with or without /tfs and a port. Use https:// where the server offers it.
config.apiVersionHint: Choose your server’s version. A server refuses versions newer than its own.
config.patHint: Sent with every call as Basic authentication. Create it for a service account rather than a person.
config.patStored: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.

errors.invalid: Enter an absolute URL, such as https://ado.contoso.local/tfs/DefaultCollection.
errors.credentials: Leave the user name and password out of the URL.

help.reqVersion: Azure DevOps Server, 2022, 2020 or 2019, installed in your network. Choose the REST API version that matches it.
help.reqPat: The server must accept personal access tokens, with IIS Basic authentication turned off. Windows sign-in (NTLM or Kerberos) is not supported.
help.reqHttps: Use HTTPS: Azure DevOps Server documents personal access tokens as working only on a server configured with HTTPS. If your server still answers on plain HTTP, turn on “Allow insecure HTTP” for this connection, which sends the token unencrypted.
help.reqTls: If the server certificate comes from an internal certificate authority, the platform must trust that authority: an administrator adds it with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.
help.reqNetwork: The platform must reach the server’s address and port, and for service hooks the server must reach the platform.
help.patTitle: How to create the personal access token
help.patStep1: Sign in to Azure DevOps Server as the account the sync should act as, for example a service account named svc-isbp.
help.patStep2: Open User settings → Personal access tokens → New Token, and pick this collection.
help.patStep3: Under Scopes, choose Custom defined and select:
help.patStep4: Paste the token above. Tokens expire: create a new one before the expiry date and paste it here.
help.hooksTitle: How to send changes as they happen (service hooks)
help.hooksIntro: Without service hooks, changes arrive with the next scheduled sync. With them, Azure DevOps tells the hub which records changed, and the hub reads them through the API.
help.hooksStep1: In each team project, open Project settings → Service hooks → Create subscription → Web Hooks.
help.hooksStep2: Create one subscription for each of these events:
help.hooksStep3: Set URL to the webhook URL shown on this connection’s overview.
help.hooksStep4: Under HTTP headers, add the webhook secret shown there:
help.hooksStep5: Set Resource details to send to Minimal, then select Test and Finish.
help.hooksNote: The hub checks the secret on every call and only uses the notification to know what to read. When you rotate the secret, update the subscriptions.
help.hooksNetwork: Service hooks are sent by Azure DevOps Server from inside your network, so the webhook URL must be reachable from the server.
